question: Can you upgrade a wastewater plant's switchgear?
html:
Yes. Wastewater-plant electrical work is a core focus for us, especially since Horton Electrical Services joined CET. Our sources don't list switchgear jobs as a separate line, so we confirm each scope on site before we quote.

What we bring

  • Wastewater relationships. Horton, announced Sep 15, 2026, brings Connecticut wastewater-plant relationships and nearly doubles our workforce (CET public filings).
  • Electrical plus efficiency. We pair Horton's electrical work with NuWave efficiency services. That matters most where aeration is the plant's biggest energy load, as at Norwalk (CET wastewater-plant targets).
  • Regional reach. We operate from Worcester, Taunton and Norwell in Massachusetts and Canton in Connecticut. We hold existing licensing in six states (CET growth plan).
  • Subcontracting at large plants. At MWRA Deer Island, our role would be electrical subcontracting plus storage and efficiency, not solar. The plant already generates 26% of its own electricity (CET wastewater-plant targets).

Where upgrades are funded

These are total project values, not electrical or switchgear scope. Our share of each would need to be estimated from the bid documents.

PlantFunded or listed projectRequested pipeline
New Haven East Shore (40 MGD)$82M wet-weather and odor control, CT FY27 fundable list$19.2M process-air compressors
Hartford WPCF (60 MGD)$24.3M sludge screening and equalization, FY26-27$31.6M pump stations
Norwalk WPCF (18 MGD)$26M final settling tanks, FY27$48M aeration system
MWRA Deer Island$289M Clarifier #2, 2026 IUPn/a

(CET wastewater-plant targets)

In Connecticut, only Table 2 and Category I items are on the fundable list. Table 3 items are requests (CET wastewater-plant targets).

What we'd need from you

  • Plant name, design flow and the equipment's age.
  • Single-line diagrams and any recent electrical study.
  • Whether the work ties to a funded capital project.

Our EPA snapshot tracks 175 plants: 65 in Connecticut, 91 in Massachusetts and 19 in Rhode Island (EPA wastewater-plant compliance snapshot). We use it for site context only. It is not a compliance assessment.

Switchgear upgrades are a way into the 62 funded or requested plant and pump-station projects behind Phase 1. They also open the door to SCADA and monitoring contracts, the recurring service mix the growth plan expects to earn a higher multiple (CET growth plan).

Next actions

  1. Pull Horton's job history to confirm switchgear jobs, typical sizes and crew capacity. No such data is in our current sources.
  2. Review bid documents for New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk. Size the electrical and switchgear share of each (est.).
  3. Build a standard switchgear site-assessment offer that leads into monitoring and efficiency work.
  4. Track Connecticut FY27 funding timing so bids line up with when awards are released.
